item.title: CoinPoker Brings the PokerGO Tour Online With $250 Million Guaranteed and $1 Million Vegas Final
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: CoinPoker’s PGT Online runs six series with $250 million guaranteed, starting with the $50M KickOff on November 8 and ending at a $1M Vegas Final.
item.content:encoded:
CoinPoker announced on October 23 that it is taking the PokerGO Tour online with PGT Online, a year-long run of six series carrying $250 million in guarantees.

The first, the $50 million PGT KickOff Online, starts November 8. The tour ends with a $1 million winner-takes-all final for 50 players at the PokerGO Studio in Las Vegas in January 2028.

Six Series Modeled on PokerGO’s Live Calendar

The KickOff is the only series with dates and guarantees so far. Five more will follow through November 2027, borrowing their names from PokerGO’s flagship live events. Online versions of the Super High Roller Bowl, the PokerGO Cup, and the PGT PLO Series are on the list, along with Poker Masters Online and a PGT Championship.

The partnership grew out of a busy few months between the two brands. CoinPoker backed High Stakes Poker’s first full week of live broadcasts in late August, then teamed up with PokerGO on a $100,000 seat giveaway for the show before teasing a November launch on X on October 19.

$50 Million KickOff Runs November 8-30

The opening series carries the same $50 million guarantee CoinPoker put on its Global Online Poker Championship in August and September. Its first headline event, the $530 PGT KickOff, guarantees $1 million on November 8. A week later, the $530 Mystery Million becomes the first Mystery Bounty tournament on CoinPoker, with bounties reaching $50,000.

Champions of the highlight events receive a physical trophy shipped to them along with a digital one in their CoinPoker Trophy Cabinet. Hundreds of other PGT Online tournaments award digital trophies and carry a Trophy Event label in the lobby.

Six highlight events headline the KickOff schedule.

PGT KickOff Online Highlight Events

Millionaire Challenges and Loyalty Badges

Vegas Final seats come through PGT Millionaire Challenges, found in the PGT Online tab of the CoinPoker app. Some challenges award a seat outright, such as winning a series Main Event. Others award a ticket to a Qualifier Tournament, where the winner takes the seat.

Players who never win a big event can still earn more shots at a seat by showing up across a series. CoinPoker counts an active day as any UTC day with at least one PGT Online tournament played. Reaching 8, 15, and 20 active days in a single series earns a Loyalty Badge and a Qualifier ticket at all three milestones, so a regular who hits them all walks away with three tickets.

Keeping a streak alive into the next series pays more, since repeating a challenge earns two Qualifier tickets and locks the earlier Badge permanently. Missing a repeat removes any Badge not yet locked, although players can start a new streak in any later series.

Rules for Vegas Final Seats

Players can hold only one Vegas Final seat. They must be 21 or older and pass CoinPoker’s KYC checks to keep it, and seats can’t be transferred or refunded. Seat holders keep earning and locking Badges in later series but no longer receive Qualifier tickets.

All 50 finalists also unlock a Finalist Journey, a set of exclusive challenges in later series that pay out upgrades and luxury add-ons for the Las Vegas trip. CoinPoker says the Finalist Journey rewards won’t include extra seats or entries and will be detailed series by series.

Vegas Final Lands a Year After the Live PGT Championship

The live PokerGO Tour crowns its 2026 champion first, when the PGT Championship returns to the PokerGO Studio on January 11-12, 2027, as a $500,000 freeroll for the season’s top 40 players and Dream Seat winners. The online final follows in the same room in January 2028, with no pay jumps and the full $1 million going to one player.

Before the KickOff opens, the High Stakes Poker giveaway wraps up on October 31, when eight weekly winners meet at a final table to decide who takes the seat.

Image: Courtesy of coinpoker.com

item.title: Adrian Mateos Takes Purple Jacket as 10 Poker Masters Events Produce 10 Winners
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Adrian Mateos won the 2026 Poker Masters Purple Jacket with 451 points in a series where all 10 events went to different players.
item.content:encoded:
Adrian Mateos won the 2026 Poker Masters Purple Jacket at the PokerGO Studio in Las Vegas on Friday, October 23, finishing the 10-event series on top of the leaderboard with 451 PGT points.

His lead survived the $51,000 finale once Jeremy Ausmus, the only player left in range, went out in fourth. Mateos also collects a $25,000 PGT Passport along with the jacket.

Ten Events, Ten Different Champions

Myles Mullaly won the $10,500 opener on October 13, and no one who followed him to the winner’s circle had been there before at this year’s series. Daniyal Gheba and Sam Laskowitz were the only players to reach the final top 10 without a title.

Justin Vaysman took Event #6 after falling to a quarter of a big blind, a comeback that ended with him beating Sean Winter heads-up.

With the trophies spread across the field, the leaderboard rewarded players who added deep runs around their wins, and the standings stayed close until the final day.

2026 Poker Masters Event Winners

Mateos Built His Lead Early

Mateos made his first final table count, finishing second to Palma in Event #2 for $151,200. He then beat Nick Schulman heads-up to win Event #5 for $229,500, and fourth place in Event #7 added another $87,000.

He also went out on the stone bubble five times. His pocket aces were cracked one spot short of the money in the opener, and he missed out by a single place again in Events #3 and #4. His fifth bubble came in Event #9, the $26,000 event Seward won by beating Daniel Negreanu heads-up. Mateos didn’t cash after Event #7, so Events #8 through #10 went by without him adding a point.

Seward’s Event #9 win lifted him to third, and the top three stayed in that order through the finale.

2026 Poker Masters Final Leaderboard Top 10

Ausmus Needed Second in the Finale

Ausmus started the finale eighth on the series leaderboard, with only a top-two finish good enough to carry him past Mateos. The Event #7 winner made it through the bubble and into the final four.

His run ended when Winter’s ace-king of diamonds caught an ace on both the turn and the river against Ausmus’ pocket fives. Fourth place paid $170,500 and settled the jacket for Mateos.

Winter Wins the Finale for $620,000

Winter, the 2022 Purple Jacket winner, went on to beat Laskowitz heads-up for the $620,000 top prize. The finale drew 31 entries for a $1,550,000 prize pool, and Laskowitz’s $387,500 for second was the best live score of his career.

Winter’s second PGT title of the season lifted him to 2,223 points on the season-long PGT leaderboard, and no other player has reached 2,000 this year.

PGT Sprint Up Next at the PokerGO Studio

Ausmus also gained ground in the Player of the Year race, climbing to third on the season leaderboard with 1,812 points after his fourth-place finish. Mateos sits sixth on 1,760.

The race for the PGT Championship picks up again on October 27, when the PGT Sprint brings seven single-day tournaments to the PokerGO Studio through November 4, with buy-ins from $5,300 to $10,500. Points from the Sprint count toward the top-40 places in the PGT Championship, a $500,000 freeroll set for January 11-12, 2027.

Image: Courtesy of pgt.com

item.title: WPT Venetian Fall Festival Opens Oct. 28 With Bag-and-Done $2 Million Championship
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: The $5,000 WPT Venetian Fall Championship runs Nov. 5-10 with a $2 million guarantee, bag-and-done flights, and $550 satellites rewarding 200,000 chips.
item.content:encoded:
The World Poker Tour heads back to The Venetian Resort Las Vegas on Wednesday, Oct. 28, as the WPT Venetian Las Vegas Fall Festival opens a series carrying nearly $4 million in guarantees through Nov. 15. Its centerpiece, the $5,000 WPT Venetian Las Vegas Fall Championship, gets underway Nov. 5 with a $2 million guarantee as one of the final championship stops of the WPT season.

Players who sat down for the spring edition will find the room working a little differently this time, from the way the cards reach them to how the starting flights are run.

Spring Championship Drew 488 Entries

The Spring Championship gave the Venetian plenty to build on in February, drawing 488 entries at the same $5,000 buy-in and pushing the prize pool to $2,244,800. Nick Seward came through heads-up against Greg Brown to take $418,700 and his first WPT title, and the fall edition now puts the same $2 million guarantee on the line with the WPT World Championship following at Wynn Las Vegas in December.

Since Seward’s win, the Venetian has changed how its cards are dealt. Two weeks before the festival, the room switched all 50 of its tables to slide dealing and became the first poker room on the Strip to stop pitching cards. Dealers now push cards flat across the felt to guard against hidden cameras, and the Fall Festival will be the first major Strip series played entirely under the new method.

Planning Around Bag-and-Done Flights

Players mapping out their week should look closely at how the starting days work. The Championship runs three starting flights at 11:10 a.m. from Nov. 5 to Nov. 7, and re-entry is unlimited within a flight until Level 9 begins. Once a player bags chips, their tournament is tied to that stack, with no option to register for a later flight or surrender chips to start again.

In practice, a player who builds a stack on Thursday is committed to it and can’t come back on Friday or Saturday looking for a bigger one. Stacks start at 50,000 under a big blind ante, and levels last an hour from the first hand until heads-up, when they drop to 30 minutes. Tables go from nine-handed to eight-handed when the field returns for Day 2 on Nov. 8, and one in eight entries will reach the money.

Entrants need to be 21 or older and hold a Venetian Rewards card to play the Championship or its satellites. The WPT is also asking players to complete the Season 24 Player Release Form in the WPT App before they arrive.

Satellites Reward a Big Stack

Players looking for a cheaper way into the Championship have plenty of satellite opportunities in the days before Day 1C. The $550 Milestone satellites run at 5:10 p.m. and 8:10 p.m. from Nov. 4 to Nov. 6. A two-seat turbo at 10:10 a.m. on Nov. 7 gives late arrivals one last shot an hour before the final flight opens.

Any player who reaches 200,000 chips in those satellites takes a Championship seat immediately and leaves the game. The remaining seats go to whoever is left once the field shrinks to match them. Earlier in the festival, $140 Milestone satellites from Oct. 28 to Oct. 31 each guarantee five seats into the $1,100 Event #4 and its $500,000 guarantee.

Guarantees Around the Championship

The Championship sits in the middle of a schedule built for both early arrivals and players staying on after the final table, with $400 bounty events carrying $15,000 guarantees on most evenings.

WPT Venetian Las Vegas Fall Festival 2026 Key Events

Final Table on PokerGO, Then Wynn

Day 3 on Nov. 9 plays down to six players, who return at 11 a.m. on Nov. 10 to play for a WPT title and a place on the Mike Sexton WPT Champions Cup. The final table streams on PokerGO from noon local time, broadcast from the studio inside the Venetian Poker Room.

Alongside the trophy, first place includes a $10,400 seat in the WPT World Championship at Wynn Las Vegas, where the season finale’s Day 1 flights begin Dec. 13.

item.title: This Week in Poker: October 19–23, 2026
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Seward beats Negreanu at the Poker Masters, two Lithuanians win big in Jeju, GGPoker bans third-party tools, and more from October 19–23.
item.content:encoded:
The Poker Masters added three more names to its 2026 winners’ list this week, and Friday’s finale will decide who leaves Las Vegas in the Purple Jacket.

Away from the PokerGO Studio, Jeju, Northern Cyprus, and Michigan all crowned champions. GGPoker also gave its players a new set of rules for the software on their machines.

Let’s take a look at what went down.

Seward Denies Negreanu for First PGT Title

Nicholas Seward claimed the biggest prize of the week at the Poker Masters on Thursday, beating Daniel Negreanu heads-up in the $26,000 Event #9. Negreanu began the final table as chip leader, but Seward moved in front with quad kings and finished the match with king-jack against king-ten. The $412,500 win was his first PGT title.

Seward now sits third in the Purple Jacket race on 397 points, behind Adrian Mateos on 451 and Nicholas Palma on 407. Negreanu took $262,500 for second, his biggest score of the series.

Lithuanian Bracelet Winners Close Out KPC Poker in Jeju

The KPC Poker October Series wrapped up at LES A Casino with two Lithuanians taking its biggest late titles. Marius Kudzmanas won the $15,000 King’s Main Event for $533,800. A day later, Rokas Asipauskas took the $30,000 Final Coronation for $300,800. His king-nine of spades caught up against Mehdi Chaoui’s pair and flush draw four-handed. He then needed just one heads-up hand to beat Dingxiang Ong.

Dutch pro Michel Molenaar came second to Yan Wen Yee in the $5,000 King’s Debut for $150,000, despite holding the chip lead heads-up, and then answered with two titles of his own. He won the $15,000 King’s Single Day High Roller Turbo for $168,400, then rivered a full house with pocket fours against ace-deuce to take the $25,000 Super High Roller for $140,000. His three biggest scores in Jeju came to $458,400.

Kolev Runs the Table at WPT Prime Cyprus

Bulgaria’s Ivelin Kolev won the $1,100 WPT Prime Cyprus Championship in Kyrenia on Monday after sitting shortest of the final five with around 18 big blinds. Pocket aces held to double him up, and nobody else at the table survived a clash with him from there. Said Tahar was the last to go, beaten by a rivered seven-high straight after 13 hands of heads-up.

The championship drew 953 entries across five starting flights against a $1 million guarantee. Kolev’s $171,600 first prize includes a $10,400 seat in the WPT World Championship at Wynn Las Vegas in December.

Ozturk Climbs to the Top of the MSPT Money List

Umut Ozturk added the MSPT Spade Poker Championship at FireKeepers Casino in Battle Creek, Michigan, to the Ohio title he won in February. The $1,110 Main Event drew 2,442 entries and built a $2,367,240 prize pool on a $1 million guarantee. Ozturk and Greg Wiggins agreed an even deal heads-up worth $280,290 apiece on Monday, and Ozturk’s small chip edge gave him the trophy.

The result was his best career score and his third MSPT title. The two-time Player of the Year now leads the tour’s all-time money list with $1,337,177.

Mateos and Vaysman Collect Poker Masters Trophies

Mateos opened his account at the series in Event #5, beating Nick Schulman heads-up for $229,500 after bubbling three of the first four events. The Spaniard was the fifth different champion in as many events, and the points from that win and his Event #2 runner-up finish carried him to the top of the Purple Jacket standings.

Justin Vaysman pulled off the comeback of the series two days later. Five-handed at the Event #6 final table, he was down to 20,000 chips, a quarter of a big blind, before a string of double-ups carried him to heads-up against Sean Winter. A rivered full house with ten-nine closed it out and earned Vaysman $192,000 and his maiden PGT trophy.

GGPoker Tightens Up Its Client

GGPoker players can no longer keep any outside poker software or automation tool open while they play. HUDs and trackers now fall under the ban too. PokerTracker 4, Hand2Note, Hold’em Manager 3, and Jurojin are among the programs named, and all of them must be shut down before the client opens.

The new security package comes after compromised third-party software let an attacker watch high-stakes players’ screens and hole cards in September. Players also get an optional Screen Guard that hides tables and hole cards from screenshots and screen sharing, and GGPoker has added win-rate anomaly checks on its side. Support for Windows 7, 8, and 8.1, and for macOS 11 and earlier, ends in 2027.

On the Calendar

The PokerGO Studio barely pauses after the Poker Masters before the PGT Sprint begins. Seven single-day tournaments run there from October 27 to November 4, with buy-ins from $5,300 to $10,500.

Rozvadov hosts its first WSOP Super Circuit from October 28 to November 11, with 18 ring events and €5 million in total guarantees. King’s Resort is no stranger to WSOP gold, having staged nine editions of WSOP Europe. Its Super Circuit schedule peaks with a €3,000 Main Event guaranteeing €2 million from November 5. Jeju is busy again the same week, as the Jeju Poker Festival returns to LES A Casino from October 28 to November 11 with 123 trophy events.

Later in the month, the Irish Open makes its Moroccan debut at Casino de Marrakech from November 10 to 15. The 36-event festival’s €1,155 Main Event starts on November 11 with a €500,000 guarantee.

item.title: Nick Seward Beats Daniel Negreanu Heads-Up to Win Poker Masters Event #9 for $412,500
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Nicholas Seward beat Daniel Negreanu heads-up in 2026 Poker Masters Event #9, winning $412,500 and his first PokerGO Tour title on Oct. 22.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Seward won Event #9: $26,000 No-Limit Hold’em at the 2026 Poker Masters on Thursday, October 22, beating Daniel Negreanu heads-up at the PokerGO Studio in Las Vegas.

The American earned $412,500 and 248 PGT points for his first PokerGO Tour title. Negreanu, who started the final table as chip leader, took $262,500 for second.

Seward Adds First PGT Title to Strong 2026

Seward already owned a World Series of Poker bracelet from 2024 and $4.7 million in Hendon Mob earnings before the penultimate event of the series. In February, he topped 488 entries to win the $5,000 WPT Venetian Las Vegas Spring Championship for $418,700.

He reached the final five of Event #2, which Nicholas Palma went on to win, and Event #9 was his fourth cash of the festival. His $578,500 in series winnings is the most of anyone in the top 10 of the standings.

Seward and Negreanu Share the Eliminations

Fifty entries at $26,000 built a $1,250,000 prize pool, the largest of the series to that point, and the top eight finishers were paid. Adrian Mateos finished on the bubble for the fifth time at this year’s Poker Masters. David Coleman’s exit in eighth then set the seven-player final table.

Every bust from there went to one of the two finalists. Jesse Lonis returned as the shortest stack and went first, his king-queen losing to Seward’s jack-nine after a jack on the turn gave Seward trips. Seward’s pocket jacks then held against Brandon Wilson’s ace-deuce of clubs and left Wilson with about a big blind.

Negreanu finished this month’s Super High Roller Bowl champion in sixth, his pocket kings beating Wilson’s queen-seven in a three-way pot. Sean Perry went next, his eight-six of clubs unable to catch Negreanu’s pocket jacks on a ten-seven-three flop with two clubs. Negreanu’s king-ten then made top pair against Matthew Wantman’s ace-queen for fourth.

Daniyal Gheba, runner-up to Joey Weissman in Event #3, lost most of his stack to Negreanu before Seward’s ace-queen beat his king-six in third. The $175,000 score moved Gheba up to fifth in the series standings on 348 points from five cashes.

Seward Works His Way Past Negreanu

Negreanu began heads-up holding 4,200,000 chips to Seward’s 3,305,000 and won the first few big pots. Seward pulled level by picking off a Negreanu bluff, then took the lead for the first time when he flopped quad kings against two pair. His rivered full house against Negreanu’s rivered flush extended that lead, though Negreanu folded the river both times.

On the final hand, Negreanu three-bet all in with king-ten over Seward’s open, and Seward called with king-jack. The nine-three-three flop left Negreanu a few ways to split the pot. The five on the turn and seven on the river kept Seward’s jack kicker in front.

Second place moved the Poker Hall of Famer up to 33rd on the season-long PGT leaderboard on 1,052 points. Wilson’s sixth place was enough to lift him to fourth on that leaderboard, now on 1,761 points.

2026 Poker Masters Event #9: $26,000 No-Limit Hold’em Results

Purple Jacket Race Goes to the Finale

Seward’s 397 points put him third in the Purple Jacket standings. Mateos leads on 451 after winning Event #5, and Palma sits second on 407. The player with the most points after all 10 events takes the jacket and a $25,000 PGT Passport, and Event #10: $51,000 NLH will settle it.

The result also took Seward to 51st on the PGT season leaderboard. The top 40 eligible players qualify for the $500,000 PGT Championship freeroll on January 11–12, 2027, subject to minimum cash requirements.

Event #10 plays to a winner on Friday, October 23, a year after Wilson took the series finale for $464,000. The tour then stays in the same room for the PGT Sprint, seven single-day tournaments from October 27 to November 4 with buy-ins from $5,300 to $10,500.

Image: Courtesy of pgt.com

item.title: Kgbseven Claims Eighth CoinMillion Title and $120,500 on CoinPoker
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Kgbseven won the eighth $215 CoinMillion on CoinPoker for $120,500 from 4,891 entries as CoinPoker teased a November PokerGO launch.
item.content:encoded:
Kgbseven won the $215 CoinMillion on CoinPoker on Monday, October 19, and collected $120,500 at the end of a two-day event that drew 4,891 entries on Sunday. The $1 million guaranteed tournament was the eighth edition of the CoinMillion. It was also the first since CoinPoker moved its flagship event to a weekly Sunday slot.

Kgbseven’s First Recorded Cash

Kgbseven had barely played tournaments on CoinPoker before this run and had no cashes on record since the site’s software overhaul in March. The account fired three $215 entries on Sunday and went on to take the title the following day.

Along with the money, every CoinMillion champion receives a physical trophy, a digital trophy in the CoinPoker Trophy Cabinet, and a place in the CoinMillion Hall of Champions. Kgbseven joins a list started by DaniC1994, who won the inaugural edition in May for $126,500. The second name on it is monc, who took $121,500 when the event returned in July.

Final Table Results

Sunday’s field played down to the last seven, who returned on Monday to finish the tournament.

$215 CoinMillion( 1M GTD) Final Table Results, October 18-19, 2026

CoinMillion’s Path to Weekly Sundays

CoinPoker first ran the CoinMillion as a one-off during its World Poker Masters series, where the May 10 debut attracted 4,278 entries. The event returned on July 12 to open the Battle of Malta Online. Those two editions combined for 9,062 entries before CoinPoker gave the tournament a monthly slot starting August 9.

Every Sunday in September brought another CoinMillion during the Global Online Poker Championship, before the event settled into its new weekly slot in October. Each edition starts players with 100,000 chips, worth 200 big blinds, on 10-minute levels. Entry is $215 direct, and daily satellites offer cheaper routes in, from freeroll steps up to direct seat events priced between $5.50 and $44.

CoinPoker and PokerGO Set November Start

On the day Kgbseven won, CoinPoker posted a teaser on X that read “It all begins this November. Coming soon.” The clip that came with it points to a year of tournaments with PokerGO, built around a PokerGO Tour–themed online series.

It all begins this November. Coming soon… https://t.co/5KMSMbDdHF

— CoinPoker (@CoinPoker_OFF) October 19, 2026

On the live PokerGO Tour, players earn points in high-stakes events through the year. The top 40 on the leaderboard and select Dream Seat winners qualify for the season-ending PGT Championship, a freeroll. The 2026 edition plays at the PokerGO Studio on January 11 and 12, 2027, with a $250,000 prize package for the winner.

High Stakes Poker Seat Race Nears Its Finish

CoinPoker already works with PokerGO through High Stakes Poker. It served as presenting sponsor when the show ran seven straight days of live streams from August 25 to 31, a first for the long-running cash game. The two brands followed up with a promotion offering one CoinPoker player a $100,000 seat on the show, decided through weekly leaderboards across cash games and tournaments.

The last leaderboard closes on Sunday, October 25, the same day the next CoinMillion kicks off at 16:30 UTC with another $1 million guarantee. Eight weekly winners then meet at a final table on October 31, where one of them takes the High Stakes Poker seat.

Image: @CoinPoker_OFF / X

item.title: Bracelet Winner Rokas Asipauskas Takes KPC Final Coronation for $300,800
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: WSOP bracelet winner Rokas Asipauskas won the $30,000 KPC Final Coronation in Jeju for $300,800, a day after Marius Kudzmanas took the King’s Main Event.
item.content:encoded:
Lithuania’s Rokas Asipauskas banked $300,800 on Wednesday, October 21, winning the $30,000 Final Coronation as the KPC Poker October Series wrapped up in Jeju, South Korea. Heads-up against Dingxiang Ong lasted one hand, and the title landed 24 hours after countryman Marius Kudzmanas claimed the $15,000 King’s Main Event for $533,800.

Two WSOP Bracelet Winners Take Jeju’s Biggest Late Titles

Neither Lithuanian was short on recent WSOP success. Asipauskas picked up his first bracelet in the Bahamas at the 2025 WSOP Paradise, where he took the $5,000 Super Colossus and $504,950 by defeating Alex Keating. Kudzmanas followed in April by winning the 2026 WSOPE Main Event in Prague for €2,000,000.

Kudzmanas got Lithuania on the board in Jeju first. Seventh in chips when the King’s Main Event final table began, he worked past a lineup that included Martin Sedlak and Tony Lin and finished on top of 169 entries and a $2,372,760 prize pool. Peng Huang, already a KPC Main Event champion earlier in the series, was his last opponent and settled for $350,000.

Asipauskas Builds Toward the Final Coronation

Asipauskas had come close twice before his win, reaching two earlier final tables in the series. His eighth-place finish in the KRW 5,000,000 High Roller paid KRW 20,500,000, roughly $15,280, and he added $43,000 for sixth in the $20,000 Crown Hunt, one spot ahead of Kudzmanas, who collected $37,000 for seventh.

Play in the $30,000 event began October 20, with each player receiving 500,000 chips and levels running 40 minutes. Twenty-five entries came in over the two days, creating a $702,000 prize pool. Asipauskas reached the last nine with 3,355,000 chips, trailing only Paulius Plausinaitis on 3,845,000.

Four-Handed All-In Turns the Final Table

The key pot came with four players left, and Mehdi Chaoui was ahead when the chips went in. His nine-six gave him a pair and a flush draw on a six-queen-ace flop carrying three hearts, while Asipauskas had shoved king-nine of spades. Asipauskas paired his nine on the turn and caught a king on the river for the better two pair, ending Chaoui’s run in fourth.

Plausinaitis went out next in third, and Asipauskas carried an 11 million to 1.3 million chip lead into heads-up. Ong shoved his last chips with the ace-ten of diamonds and ran into the king-eight of diamonds. Asipauskas flopped a pair of eights, and the rest of the 89652 board gave Ong nothing.

Ong was no stranger to big titles himself. The Singaporean beat 1,974 entries to win the Poker Dream Main Event at Resorts World Genting in April 2025.

Prize money went to the final four players only.

KPC Poker October Series $30,000 Final Coronation Results

Jeju Poker Festival Opens October 28

The October series was the first major stop since K Poker Cup and King Poker Cup merged into the single KPC Poker brand.

Players won’t wait long for more action at LES A Casino, as the Jeju Poker Festival starts there on October 28 and runs until November 11.

KPC Poker shares organizing duties with the Red Dragon Poker Tour across a 15-day schedule of 123 trophy events. A KRW 880 million guarantee sits on the opening KPC Main Event, and the Red Dragon Plus Championship carries KRW 1.8 billion guaranteed when it finishes the festival on November 11.

Over in Incheon, WPT Seoul overlaps with the festival from October 30 to November 9 at INSPIRE Entertainment Resort.

Image: Courtesy of kpclive.com

item.title: Asian Poker Tour Online Tops $5.74 Million as Guarantees Outpace Turnout
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Guarantees climbed 26.42% while pools grew 6.5% through eight APT Online trophy events, setting up a $5 million Main Event on Natural8.
item.content:encoded:
Natural8 players have built $5.74 million in prize pools across the first eight trophy events of Asian Poker Tour Online (APT Online) 2026, 6.5% more than the same events paid in 2025. Entries grew 2.5% to 25,224, while Natural8 raised the guarantees on those events by 26.42%.

A $40 Million APT Online Series After 18 Record-Setting Events

APT Online, the online branch of the Asian Poker Tour (APT), runs October 11 to November 2 on Natural8 with $40 million in guarantees, up 60% from the $25 million behind the 2025 edition.

The schedule has 20 trophy events, and each winner collects a trophy plus a $10,000 seat to the APT Championship Main Event in Taipei. Last year’s edition paid out $42.81 million across 381 tournaments and, by Natural8’s count, set records in 18 of its 20 trophy events, with entries up 48.4% and prize money up 51.8% on the 2024 edition.

Two live festivals ran just before it. APT Incheon ran August 7 to 16 at Paradise City in Incheon, South Korea, and APT Jeju closed on October 7 after awarding about $14.6 million (KRW 19.4 billion) in prize money.

Six of Eight Events Set Records, Led by a $356,853 Mystery Bounty Score

Eight trophy events in, the series stands at 25,224 entries and $5.74 million in prize pools, according to the operator’s recap of Events #5 through #8. Six of the eight set new APT Online benchmarks, and Natural8 measures each tournament against its 2025 edition.

Natural8 reports the Thailand and Taiwan National Cup pools in local currency, so those dollar figures are approximate conversions.

Valen_tina of the United Arab Emirates took the series’ biggest payday to date. The $250 Mystery Bounty Hunter drew a 9,321-entry field and a $2.14 million prize pool, and Valen_tina collected $156,443 for first place plus $200,410 in mystery bounties, a $356,853 total.

Avdi_2000 of Austria earned the largest first-place prize of the series so far, $205,728, by winning the $5,000 Superstar Challenge from a 246-entry field. milka29, also from Austria, won the $1,050 High Roller and its Rose Gold Mega Lion trophy for $119,682 after finishing ninth in the Taiwan National Cup earlier in the series.

The Taiwan National Cup used a bounty format for the first time and built a $293,454 pool, 26.9% above 2025. MoneyMaker_1999 of China won $28,349 including bounties, and the 2,904-entry field fell short of the 3,134 entries the 2025 edition drew.

Event #4 debuted as a Single Day High Roller Bounty Freezeout, replacing last year’s Double Stack, and its 722 entries beat the $300,000 guarantee by 20.33%.

Renato Pozzetto of Slovenia won the $100 Turbo Ultra Stack, beating Andre Figueiredo of Brazil heads-up after about seven hours of play.

The Cheaper High Roller Drew 32% More Entries and Built a Smaller Pool

Entries set the High Roller’s record. Natural8 cut the buy-in from $1,500 to $1,050, and entries jumped 32.39% from 636 in 2025 to 842. The prize pool still slipped 7.09% to $842,000, and the top prize fell 11.32%.

Turbo Ultra Stack entries followed a similar pattern, rising 28.13% to 3,475, a record for the event, while the $319,700 prize pool grew just 2.51%.

Natural8 lifted the combined guarantees on the eight tournaments by 26.42%, from $3.61 million to $4.56 million. The pools cleared those targets by roughly 26% this year, against about 49% for the same events in 2025.

Growth has not caught up with the new guarantees yet. The 12 events after Event #8 will test Natural8’s bet, with the $5 million Main Event the largest wager.

$5 Million Main Event and a Taipei Seat for Every Winner

Last year’s $800 Main Event drew 5,680 entries and built a $4.32 million pool, and Oscar Cueva of Peru took the title for $601,336. This year’s guarantee jumps from $3 million to $5 million.

Another 5,680 entries at the same buy-in would leave the pool about $683,000 short of the new guarantee. Covering it takes roughly 16% more entries than last year, well above the 2.5% growth the series has shown so far.

The series also feeds the APT Championship in Taipei. Winners of all 20 trophy events earn a $10,000 seat to the $5 million Main Event, which starts November 23, so the eight champions have already claimed seats worth $80,000. Satellites run through November 23 from $12.

Mini Main Event Defends a 15,150-Entry Record on October 25

Two more events land this week. A $525 Single Day High Roller Double Stack with a $400,000 guarantee starts October 22 at 12:00 UTC (8 p.m. HKT), and the $80 Mini Main Event with a $1 million guarantee plays its final day October 25.

A 15,150-entry field at a $100 buy-in made last year’s Mini Main Event the largest in APT Online history, with a $1.39 million pool. A bigger turnout at the lower price would show the series growing faster than its early 2.5% pace.

Both the Super High Roller and the Main Event play November 1, and a $100,000 freeroll for APT Online players follows on November 7.

item.title: Umut Ozturk Wins MSPT Spade Poker Championship for $280,290
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Umut Ozturk won the MSPT Spade Poker Championship at FireKeepers Casino, moving to the top of the tour’s all-time money list with $1,337,177.
item.content:encoded:
Umut Ozturk won the 2026 MSPT Spade Poker Championship at FireKeepers Casino in Battle Creek, Michigan, closing out the final day early on Monday, October 19. He and Greg Wiggins split the top two prizes evenly for $280,290 each, the largest score of Ozturk’s career.

FireKeepers Draws 2,442 Entries

The second edition of the $1,110 event drew 525 entries on Day 1A, 859 on Day 1B, and 1,058 on Day 1C. The 2,442 entries built a $2,367,240 prize pool against a $1 million guarantee, and all 266 players who returned for Day 2 were in the money with at least $2,553.

Ozturk was one of four players to bag chips in two flights, and he started the final day with a top-20 stack. He had pocket aces cracked early on Day 2 but kept enough chips to reach the final nine.

Season 17 Player of the Year points leader Mike Wilklow went out in 136th for $3,250, and defending champion Merritt Kuhn took 40th for $6,685. Jennifer Lin was the last woman standing, finishing 18th for $18,570.

Wiggins Takes Over the Final Table

Derek Gregory made two of the first three eliminations at the final table, sending out Randy Froelich in ninth and Frank Lagodich in seventh. Reigning Player of the Year Jake Long went out in eighth, a result that moved him up to third in this season’s points race.

Wiggins, from Elmira, Michigan, then took control. He eliminated two-time bracelet winner Scott Bohlman in sixth when his ace-five beat eight-deuce suited, then doubled through Gregory when his ace-eight of spades turned trip aces against pocket kings. A flip with pocket queens against Dan Sepiol’s ace-king of diamonds gave him the chip lead. Gregory, who had held a third of the chips five-handed, went out in fifth when Wiggins rivered a set of deuces against his ace-queen.

Gian Bencivenga’s ace-six of hearts dominated Sepiol’s ten-six to end Sepiol’s run in fourth for $123,028, his 19th MSPT Main Event cash. Bencivenga then moved in with king-queen of spades from the small blind against Ozturk’s ace-four of diamonds, and the board missed him, leaving him third for $164,811.

Heads-up started with the stacks close to even. After a few hands, Ozturk and Wiggins agreed to split the remaining money equally, with Ozturk holding slightly more chips and taking the title.

2026 MSPT Spade Poker Championship Final Table Results

*Heads-up deal

Ozturk Moves to the Top of the MSPT Money List

The result lifted the St. Paul, Minnesota, player to first on the MSPT career earnings list with $1,337,177. It was his 19th final table and 75th cash on the tour, and his third MSPT title.

Two of those titles have come this season, after he won the Ohio Poker State Championship at JACK Cleveland in February. His first came at the 2023 Missouri State Championship at Hollywood Casino near St. Louis, and the MSPT Hall of Famer is also a two-time Player of the Year on the tour.

Ozturk left FireKeepers during the tour’s May stop after his mother was diagnosed with terminal cancer, and she died a couple of months later. “Even though she wasn’t here with me physically, I felt her the entire weekend, so this one is dedicated to my mother,” he told the MSPT after the win.

The Season Finale Moves to Florida

The MSPT moves on to Grand Falls Casino in Larchwood, Iowa, from October 28 to November 1. Every 2026 MSPT Main Event champion earns a seat in the $3,500, $2 million guaranteed MSPT Championship at Seminole Hard Rock Hollywood, part of the Rock ’N’ Roll Poker Open that runs November 17 to December 2.

The championship awards 1.5 times the usual Player of the Year points. Ozturk earned his seat with the Ohio win in February.

Image: Courtesy of msptpoker.com

item.title: Ivelin Kolev Wins WPT Prime Cyprus Championship for $171,600
item.dc:creator: James Thompson
item.description: Ivelin Kolev went from the shortest stack five-handed to WPT Prime Cyprus champion, eliminating the final four players for $171,600.
item.content:encoded:
Bulgaria’s Ivelin Kolev won the $1,100 WPT Prime Cyprus Championship at the Chamada Prestige Hotel & Spa in Kyrenia, Northern Cyprus, on Monday, October 19, beating Said Tahar heads-up for $171,600. He was the shortest stack at the table with five players left and went on to eliminate every remaining opponent.

Kolev Starts the Final Day Fourth of Eight

The championship drew 953 entries across five starting flights from October 15 to 19 and carried a $1 million guarantee. The festival followed the $3,500 WPT Cyprus Championship at the same venue in August.

Eight players returned for the livestreamed final day. Kolev sat fourth with 4,525,000, behind Tahar on 12,000,000, Andreas Christodoulo on 7,750,000, and Bora Kurtulus on 5,425,000. Ismail Yagci started shortest on 950,000.

After Yagci and Sergiu Cornea went out, Kurtulus opened pocket aces under the gun and Joseph El Khoury called with king-jack. The jack on the turn gave El Khoury two pair, and he called Kurtulus’ check-jam for 4,150,000 after a long think to send him out in sixth.

Pocket Aces Lift Kolev Off the Bottom

Five-handed, El Khoury led with 11,250,000 and Kolev was the shortest stack on 5,500,000, around 18 big blinds. Christodoulo, just above him on 5,575,000, won two pots from Tahar over the next 11 hands, including a check-jam with flopped two pair.

A dozen hands after those counts, Kolev picked up pocket aces. Tahar opened with king-ten, Kolev called in the cutoff, and Johan Storakers moved all in from the button with pocket nines. Tahar folded, Kolev called off his 5,100,000 stack, and the aces held to put him on 11,600,000.

Storakers rebuilt by doubling through El Khoury with king-queen against king-jack, but Kolev then knocked out two players on consecutive hands. His pocket fives held against Storakers’ ace-six for fifth place, and his queen-jack flopped a pair against Christodoulo’s pocket fives to end his run in fourth.

On the next hand, Kolev flopped the nut straight with nine-eight on seven-six-five and bet every street against El Khoury, who folded to his river shove. Kolev moved to 25,300,000 chips, with El Khoury on 6,400,000.

Kolev Closes Out Tahar Heads-Up

Three-handed, Kolev’s trip fours beat El Khoury’s two pair to take his stack past 26 million. Two hands later, he flopped the nut flush with king-nine of diamonds and picked up another pot when El Khoury folded to his river bet. El Khoury called off his last 2,200,000 with king-four against Kolev’s button shove with queen-ten, and the ten on the turn sent him out in third for $74,000.

Kolev took 32,950,000 into heads-up play against Tahar’s 5,175,000. Tahar’s only double came when a jack on the river rescued his jack-ten against Kolev’s ace-four. Kolev won the next pot with a turn bet to reach 32,275,000 against 5,850,000, and the match lasted 13 hands in total.

On the final hand, Kolev limped the button, Tahar called, and both checked a flop of ten-seven-five with three clubs. Kolev bet the queen on the turn and Tahar called. The three on the river gave Tahar two pair with queen-three and completed a seven-high straight for Kolev’s six-four. Tahar called Kolev’s shove for his last 2,950,000.

The win was worth 900 WPT Player of the Year points to Kolev, with Tahar earning 700 for second.

2026 WPT Prime Cyprus Championship Final Table Results

*Includes $10,400 WPT World Championship seat

World Championship Seat Comes With the Title

Of Kolev’s $171,600, $10,400 comes as a seat in the WPT World Championship at Wynn Las Vegas, the December event that closes Season 24. Shrikant Pillamarapu received the same seat with his first-place money at the WPT Prime Lodge Championship in Austin a week earlier.

Before the World Championship, Wynn hosts the $1,100 WPT Prime Championship from December 5 to 12, with a $5 million guarantee.
